5fe12e7f75.fzText: FZ GRADE: Only students who have collected at least 25 points in total from the midterm exam, homework 1, homework 2, and class participation will be entitled to take the final exam
weekly: Sociological Imagination. Required Reading: C. Wright Mills, The Sociological Imagination, chapter 1 “Promise" (sections 1 and 2)
Classical Sociology: Durkheim. Required Reading: Émile Durkheim, Suicide, chapter 2 “Egoistic Suicide”
Classical Sociology: Marx. Required Reading: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, The Communist Manifesto, chapter 1 “Bourgeois and Proletarians”
Classical Sociology: Weber. Required Reading: Max Weber, The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism, chapter 5 “Asceticism and the Spirit of Capitalism”
Sociological Perspectives. Required Reading: John Macionis, Sociology, chapter 1.5 & 1.6 “Sociological Perspectives”

Globalization. Required Reading: Immanuel Wallerstein, World-System Analysis. An Introduction, chapter 2 “The Modern World-System as a Capitalist World-Economy: Production, Surplus-Value, and Polarization”
Work. Required Reading: André Gorz, Reclaiming Work, chapter 2 “The Latest Forms of Work”
Gender. Required Reading: Judith Butler, “Performative Acts and Gender Constitution: An Essay in Phenomenology and Feminist Theory” https://doi.org/10.2307/3207893.
Race, Ethnicity, Nation. Required Reading: Stuart Hall, Selected Writings on Race and Difference (edited by Paul Gilroy and Ruth Wilson Gilmore), chapter 19 “Race, the Floating Signifier"
textbooks: Required - Reading: Pdf files of individual texts for each week (available on the Moodle)
outcomes: Discuss a range of social theories and concepts
Interpret various types of media and literary work from a critical sociological lens
Select and justify basic research methods with regard to various research topics
Critically assess contemporary debates and discourses through the application of core sociological concepts
Criticise the influence of different, intersecting social structures existing in local and global society
Contextualise social issues in relation to local and wider global structures, such as nation states and globalisation
